script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Family
Theme: career transition

Begin screenplay.

FADE IN:

INT. LIVING ROOM - DAY

A FAMILY of five sits on the couch. The FATHER, mid-40s, is wearing a suit. He's holding a newspaper and looks worried. The mother, MID-30s, is knitting. The three kids, ages 11, 8, and 5, are playing board games on the floor.

FATHER
(sternly)
This is it. I've been laid off.

MOTHER
(surprised)
What does that mean?

FATHER
It means I've lost my job. I'll need to find a new one soon.

INT. KITCHEN - NIGHT

The Father is on the computer, applying for jobs. The Mother comes in and puts her arms around him.

MOTHER
I'll help you. We'll figure this out.

INT. DINING ROOM - DAY

The family sits around the table, brainstorming ideas for the Father's new career.

ELDER SON
Dad, have you considered becoming a teacher?

FATHER
(smiling)
I've thought about it, but I don't think I have the patience for that.

ELDER DAUGHTER
What about starting your own business?

FATHER
(hesitant)
I've always wanted to, but I don't know where to start.

INT. PARK - DAY

The family is having a picnic. The Father looks lost in thought. The Mother notices and gives him a reassuring smile.

MOTHER
Remember what you always said? "When one door closes, another one opens."

FATHER
(sighs)
Yes, I remember. I just hope I can find that new door soon.

INT. LIBRARY - DAY

The Father is researching potential careers. He finds a book on graphic design.

INT. LIVING ROOM - NIGHT

The Father shows the family his new discovery.

FATHER
(excitedly)
I think I want to be a graphic designer!

MOTHER
(smiling)
That's great, honey. I'm proud of you for exploring new possibilities.

INT. CLASSROOM - DAY

The Father attends his first graphic design class. He's nervous but determined.

FATHER
(to the instructor)
I'm new to this. I have a lot to learn.

INSTRUCTOR
(encouragingly)
That's okay. We all start somewhere.

INT. DINING ROOM - NIGHT

The family gathers around the table for dinner. The Father has brought home some of his new designs.

FATHER
I made these myself. What do you think?

MOTHER
(impressed)
They're beautiful, honey.

ELDER SON
(excitedly)
Dad, you're a natural!

INT. WORKSHOP - DAY

The Father is now working in his own graphic design studio. The family visits him during his first day.

ELDER DAUGHTER
(proudly)
We're so proud of you, Dad!

FATHER
(grinning)
Thank you, kids. I couldn't have done it without your support.

INT. LIVING ROOM - NIGHT

The family sits on the couch, watching TV. The Father's new career has brought a new sense of excitement to their lives.

FATHER
(looking at his family)
I'm glad we went through this transition together.

MOTHER
(smiling)
Me too, honey. Me too.

FADE OUT.
